title: Risk and protective factors for middle- and long-distance running-related injury
authors: Hulme A, Nielsen RO, Timpka T, Verhagen E, Finch C
population: 73 eligible articles on runners competing from 800 m to 42.2 km (searches 1970-2015)
findings: 73 articles included; 19 (26.0%) were of high and 30 (41.0%) of satisfactory methodological quality.
A history of previous injury was associated with increased risk of both general and specific RRI.
Irregular and/or absent menstruation was associated with increased risk of stress fracture, whereas oral contraceptive use was associated with decreased risk.
High clinical, methodological and statistical heterogeneity made pooling of effect sizes infeasible and prevented definitive conclusions for most factors.
limitations: No pooled estimates; high heterogeneity; distances up to marathon only (no ultra); mostly observational; search ended Dec 2015.
implications: Add 'injury in the last 12 months' as an onboarding/risk-profile input that makes progression more conservative; the 12-month window and the size of the adjustment are engineering choices.
Capture menstrual irregularity as a reported flag that triggers a caution to seek medical review, not a plan parameter.
No other training factor in this review justifies a rule change.

verification.notes: Crossref: Sports Med 47:869-886 (online Oct 2016). Abstract matched. Grade lowered from A to B because no pooled estimate was possible. The '12 months' window is not in the abstract.
